landing.features.rbac.description: Fine-grained RBAC with wildcard matching. Full admin panel for managing users, roles, and permissions.

landing.features.i18n.description: English and Chinese built-in with locale-aware routing. Easy to extend with additional languages.

landing.features.cms.description: Categories and posts with full CRUD, status management, and admin panel — build your blog or docs.

landing.faq.description: Everything you need to know before getting started.
landing.faq.stack.question: What's the tech stack?
landing.faq.stack.answer: Next.js 16 with the App Router, React 19, TypeScript strict mode, Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn/ui, Drizzle ORM, and better-auth. Every piece of business logic is inlined — no external packages for payment, email, storage, or AI.
landing.faq.payment.question: Which payment providers are supported?
landing.faq.payment.answer: Stripe, PayPal, Creem, Alipay, and WeChat Pay out of the box. The PaymentManager abstraction makes it straightforward to add more providers by implementing a single interface.
landing.faq.database.question: Which databases can I use?
landing.faq.database.answer: Drizzle ORM handles PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, Turso, and Cloudflare D1. Switch providers by editing DATABASE_PROVIDER in your .env — the schema templates and drizzle config adapt automatically.
landing.faq.customize.question: How customizable is the landing page?
landing.faq.customize.answer: The src/blocks/ directory ships with demo sections — they're designed to be rewritten per project. The durable primitives live in src/components/, so your rebrand touches blocks and translations, not the chassis.
landing.faq.license.question: Can I use this for commercial projects?
landing.faq.license.answer: Yes. ShipAny Next is built for shipping production SaaS products. You own the code after cloning — no per-seat fees, no runtime dependencies on our infrastructure.

landing.cta.subheadline: Stop wiring auth, payments, and RBAC from scratch. Start with ShipAny Next and build what actually makes your product unique.

photocraft.install.description: Use the official download for your system, then follow these three steps to install PhotoCraft and open your first image.
photocraft.install.windows.1.title: Download the installer
photocraft.install.windows.1.text: Use the Windows download link to get the x64 MSI installer for most Intel and AMD PCs. On a Snapdragon PC, choose the ARM64 release build under other architectures.
photocraft.install.windows.2.title: Run the setup
photocraft.install.windows.2.text: Double-click the .msi file and follow the setup prompts. Prefer no installation? Unzip the matching portable ZIP instead.
photocraft.install.windows.3.title: Open your first image
photocraft.install.windows.3.text: Launch PhotoCraft from the Start menu. Use File → Open to choose an image or a copy of your PSD document.
photocraft.install.windows.tip: If Windows shows a security warning, confirm the file came from storytold/photocraft and check its signature before continuing.
photocraft.install.macos.1.title: Get the Universal DMG
photocraft.install.macos.1.text: The official macOS download is a Universal DMG for both Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Save the disk image using the download link above.
photocraft.install.macos.2.title: Move it to Applications
photocraft.install.macos.2.text: Open the disk image and drag PhotoCraft to your Applications folder. Eject the disk image when finished.
photocraft.install.macos.3.title: Launch and start editing
photocraft.install.macos.3.text: Open PhotoCraft from Applications or Spotlight. Choose File → Open and select a picture or PSD copy to explore.
photocraft.install.macos.tip: The official DMG is signed and notarized. If macOS blocks the app, verify its source and consult the project’s release documentation.
photocraft.install.linux.1.title: Choose the right build
photocraft.install.linux.1.text: For Linux, download the x86_64 AppImage release build for most desktop PCs. ARM64 builds, Flatpak, DEB and RPM packages are available in the download section above.
photocraft.install.linux.2.title: Make it executable
photocraft.install.linux.2.text: Open a terminal in the download folder. Run the chmod command below, or allow execution in the file’s Properties dialog.
photocraft.install.linux.3.title: Run PhotoCraft
photocraft.install.linux.3.text: Run the AppImage using the second command below. Open an image with File → Open. Use your package manager for DEB or RPM.
photocraft.install.linux.tip: Wayland drag-and-drop is not supported in this release. Use File → Open or paste an image. The commands in this section are for x86_64 AppImage.

photocraft.faq.title: Before you download.
photocraft.faq.description: A little context to help you choose your next image editor.
photocraft.faq.free.a: Yes. PhotoCraft is a free, open-source image editor, and the official standalone builds do not require a subscription. The project includes MIT and Apache-2.0 license files. Bundled fonts, artwork and other assets can have separate terms, so consult the project’s attribution files if you plan to redistribute them. You can start with one desktop installer; the ArtCraft Launcher is another installation option, not a purchase required to unlock the download links on this page.
photocraft.faq.psd.a: The project documents reading and writing layered PSD and PSB files. That is useful when you want to try an existing image, but it does not promise identical handling of every Photoshop feature. Begin with a duplicate and inspect fonts, masks, effects and layer structure. Make a small change, save under a new name, then reopen the result in the application used for delivery. Keep the original file until you have checked the edited document and a flat reference export.
photocraft.faq.replacement.q: PhotoCraft vs Photoshop: which should I download?
photocraft.faq.replacement.a: Try PhotoCraft if you want a free desktop editor, access to its source code or a native Linux build. If your work depends on a specific Adobe feature, plugin or team handoff, test that requirement before switching. A familiar interface and PSD support do not establish complete compatibility. Our dedicated comparison covers licensing, platforms and a practical migration test, so you can evaluate the workflow you actually use before making a commitment.
photocraft.faq.account.q: Do I need an account or internet connection?
photocraft.faq.account.a: The standalone editor is designed to run locally without an account. You need a connection to download its installer, consult online documentation and obtain updates. After installation, begin with a local image and confirm the editing and export tasks you need. The desktop package, ArtCraft Launcher and downloadable web build have different setup steps; choose the desktop installer if your goal is simply to edit files on your computer.
photocraft.faq.updates.q: Where can I download a newer PhotoCraft version?
photocraft.faq.updates.a: Every six hours, this site compares GitHub’s latest official release with the download catalog. New filenames, sizes and SHA256 values are verified before the site builds and publishes an update automatically. A failed check keeps the last successful production deployment and opens a tracked issue for retry. The editing tests and malware scans identify their actual tested versions; an automatic download update does not repeat those tests. Before updating your installation, read the official release notes and keep copies of your projects.
photocraft.faq.official.q: Is this the official PhotoCraft website?
photocraft.faq.official.a: No. This is an independent download and getting-started guide. PhotoCraft is made by ArtCraft, and the download buttons lead to the official storytold/photocraft releases. We do not host modified installers or sell access to the software. For developer announcements, release notes and bug reports, use the official project. The guides linked here add installation explanations and workflow comparisons; they are not statements issued by ArtCraft or Adobe.

photocraft.downloads.checkMethod: Every six hours, the updater compares the official latest tag, verifies all listed files and SHA256 values, and publishes passing updates automatically.
photocraft.faq.safe.a: Use the official storytold/photocraft GitHub release or the ArtCraft product page. Our buttons link directly to those release files, without repackaging the installer. Before opening a file, confirm its name, version and architecture, then compare its SHA-256 value with the official checksum list. Keep your system’s security checks enabled. Our automated link check confirms availability and release metadata; it does not scan the software for malware or guarantee its behavior. An open-source license alone is not a security certification.
photocraft.faq.installer.q: Which PhotoCraft installer should I choose?
photocraft.faq.installer.a: Choose the download page for your operating system, then check the processor architecture and package format there. Each platform guide provides its official files, complete SHA256 values and installation steps. The macOS Universal DMG is the desktop installer; Linux offers several package formats. A CLI archive is intended for command-line use.
photocraft.faq.checksum.q: How do I verify a downloaded file?
photocraft.faq.checksum.a: Open SHA256SUMS.txt from the same official release as your installer and find the line with the exact filename. Calculate a SHA-256 checksum locally using Get-FileHash on Windows, shasum -a 256 on macOS or sha256sum on Linux. Compare the complete value, not just its beginning. If the values differ, do not run that copy: confirm you selected the matching release and download it again. A matching checksum helps verify file integrity; it does not replace checking the source or your system’s security controls.
photocraft.faq.failed.q: What if a download or first launch fails?
photocraft.faq.failed.a: Retry from the official release page and check whether the file finished downloading. Confirm the operating system, architecture and available disk space before treating a launch error as an application bug. For Linux, also check executable permissions or the package’s required runtime. Keep the exact error message and version number when asking for help. Avoid changing file extensions, disabling security checks or trying an unrelated mirror as a shortcut. The Linux guide includes package-specific steps, while the app guide covers a simple first editing session.

photocraft.chooser.help.windows: Open Settings → System → About → System type. Most Intel/AMD PCs are 64-bit; Snapdragon PCs use ARM64. Match the system type shown on your computer.
photocraft.chooser.help.macos: Open Apple menu → About This Mac. “Chip: Apple M…” means Apple silicon; “Processor: Intel…” means Intel.
photocraft.chooser.help.linux: Run uname -m in a terminal: x86_64 = Intel/AMD 64-bit, aarch64 = ARM64, riscv64 = RISC-V 64.
photocraft.chooser.modeHelp.windows: MSI installs the app. For the portable ZIP, extract the entire folder before launching.
photocraft.chooser.modeHelp.macos: macOS uses one Universal DMG for both Intel and Apple silicon. This release has no portable desktop ZIP; the CLI ZIP is a command-line tool.
photocraft.chooser.modeHelp.linux: Install: Flatpak, which needs Flatpak support. Portable: AppImage; allow it to run as a program before launching.
photocraft.chooser.modeHelp.riscv64: This release provides a tar.gz desktop archive for RISC-V 64. Extract it and follow the official Linux instructions for dependencies and launch steps.
photocraft.chooser.chooseSystem: Start by selecting your operating system.
photocraft.chooser.chooseChip: Check your chip using the tip above, then choose the matching option. We will not guess a file for you.
photocraft.chooser.chooseMode: Choose installation or portable use to see your file.
photocraft.chooser.unavailable: No matching file is listed for this combination. Check the official release files below.
photocraft.chooser.result.windows.instal: Run this MSI and follow the setup steps to install the desktop app.
photocraft.chooser.result.windows.portab: Extract the entire ZIP into a folder, then launch the app inside it. No MSI installation is needed.
photocraft.chooser.result.macos: Open the DMG and drag the app into Applications. This Universal file supports both Intel and Apple silicon Macs.
photocraft.chooser.result.linux.install: Install this package with Flatpak. If your system does not have Flatpak support, follow the Linux guide first or choose the AppImage.
photocraft.chooser.result.linux.portable: Allow this AppImage to run as a program, then launch it. See the Linux guide if your distribution needs additional dependencies.
photocraft.chooser.result.riscv64: Extract the full archive and follow the official Linux instructions to launch it. This is the desktop archive, not a source-code download.

photocraft.captures.description: Captured on 23 Oct 2026: PhotoCraft 0.14.0 x64 Portable on Windows 11 25H2, with an RTX 4060 Laptop GPU and DX12. We opened our original artwork, duplicated a layer, added Levels at 1.10, then saved and reopened this simple PSD. This check covers this file and this Windows build.
